grade.first_issue: No decisive defect; Rules A–F impose no cap. The phrase “for any n” in the orbit-approximation step should literally be “for all sufficiently large n,” but the proof immediately uses only the limit as n tends to infinity, so this is harmless.
grade.summary: The submission correctly derives the iterate relation and nonnegativity of g=f-id, proves that all positive values of g coincide by comparing nearby arithmetic-progressive orbits, excludes coexistence of defect values 0 and c using connectedness, and verifies every translation f(x)=x+c with c≥0. The argument supports the complete and correct classification.
strengths: Correctly squares the inequalities using positivity and obtains equality at x=f(y).
Correctly derives g(f(y))=g(y), the arithmetic form of forward iterates, and g≥0.
The orbit-approximation argument validly proves uniqueness of a positive value of g.
The clopen-set argument correctly rules out mixed values 0 and c.
The converse is verified by exact square identities.

errors.description: The choice of a nonnegative integer m approximating z1+nc1 by z2+mc2 is guaranteed only for sufficiently large n, not necessarily every n. This is exactly the range used in the limiting argument.
